text: Children under 15 make up a much larger share of the population in Africa and South Asia than in Europe or East Asia — birth rates in sub-Saharan Africa are roughly 4–5 times higher than in Japan
In Niger, more than half the population is under 15 — one of the youngest age structures in the world, compared to under 15% in most of Europe
36.4% of Pakistan's population consists of children aged 0–14 (under 15 years old)
24% of India's population falls within the 0–14 age bracket (under 15 years old)
"India has roughly 350 million children under 15 — more than the entire population of the United States"
28% of Bangladesh's population belongs to the 0–14 age demographic (under 15 years old)
The share of people over 65 is rising in almost every country — driven by falling birth rates and longer lives — creating new pressures on pension and healthcare systems
Japan leads the world in population ageing — nearly 30% of its population is over 65, compared to under 3% in many sub-Saharan African countries
Lagos, Dhaka, and Delhi each add millions of residents every year — cities in the global south now account for most of the world's urban population growth
In 1950 only about 30 in every 100 people lived in cities; by 2050 that figure is expected to reach 68 — urbanisation has been one of the defining shifts of the modern era
Sub-Saharan Africa is the world's fastest-urbanising region, with around 45% of its population already in cities — yet it remains less urbanised than every other major world region
India crossed 800 million internet users in 2023 — a single country now has more people online than the entire world did in 2005, reflecting how fast connectivity has spread

Internet access has grown faster than almost any technology in history — from fewer than 1 in 50 people in 1997 to a clear majority today — yet hundreds of millions remain offline, mostly in rural Africa and South Asia
Sub-Saharan Africa has the lowest internet penetration of any world region — around 40% of people were online in 2023, compared to over 90% in Europe and North America
China and India together account for roughly a third of all smartphone users on Earth — scale in just two countries that dwarfs most continents
More people now own a smartphone than have access to safely managed drinking water — consumer technology has spread faster than basic infrastructure in many regions
In sub-Saharan Africa, smartphone ownership has grown rapidly but still lags behind other regions — around 40–50% of adults owned a smartphone in 2023, compared to over 80% in Europe
The number of forcibly displaced people has more than doubled since 2012, driven by prolonged conflicts that show no sign of resolution — displacement is increasingly long-term, not temporary

Most refugees are hosted not by wealthy countries but by neighbouring low-income nations — countries like Uganda, Iran, and Colombia host millions despite having far fewer resources than European or North American states
Sudan's conflict alone has produced over 8 million internally displaced people since 2023 — a single crisis straining the entire global humanitarian system
While Europe/North america has 90% internet availability, only 40% in sub-Saharan africa have access
By 2023, India had more internet users than the number of internet users in the entire world back in 2005. In other words, internet penetration has been dramatic in the last 2 decades.
